Ajab Singh Rawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July,
2024

Author: Anand Pathak
Bench: Anand Pathak

1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At G Wa L I O R
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Anand Pathak
On The 12th Of July, 2024
Misc. Criminal Case No. 21404 of 2024

Ajab Singh Rawat
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Bhanu Pratap Singh - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Rajeev Upadhyay - Public Prosecutor for respondent/State.

Order 
1
.  The applicant has filed this second bail application u/S.439 Cr.P.C for grant of bail.

Applicant has been arrested on 17.10.2023 by Police Station- Aron, District Gwalior (M.P.), in connection with Crime No.105/2023, for the offence punishable under Sections 436, 336, 427, 506, 147, 148, 149 of IPC.
2.
It is the submission of learned counsel for applicant that applicant is suffering confinement since 17.10.2023 and charge sheet in the case has already been filed.
Learned counsel for applicant placed different bail orders passed in case of different co-accused and seeks parity.

Even otherwise,
applicant has already suffered around 9 months of incarceration and learnt the lesson hard way and would mend his ways by not involving in any criminal activities in future.
He further undertakes to remain outside the vicinity of village where the complainant's side reside so as to dispel the fear of complainant of backlash.
He further undertakes to perform community service to purge his misdeeds, if any.
Under these grounds, he prayed for bail 3.

Per contra, learned Pubic Prosecutor for the respondent/State opposed the prayer on the ground that applicant bears criminal record of seven cases in which one case was of offence under Section 376 of IPC and other were of arson.
Therefore, either bail be rejected or stringent condition be imposed.

sentences.text: 4. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the case diary.

5. Considering the submissions specially the period of custody and the factum of parity vis-a-vis other co-accused persons who have been granted benefit of bail, this Court intends to allow the application but looking to the nature of dispute and allegations against applicant with certain stringent condition.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.

The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be;
7.
The applicant shall not move in the vicinity and village limit where the complainant resides till conclusion of trial so that complainant may not have the fear of backlash.
8. Applicant shall not try to contact with complainant side either in person through somebody or through electronic mode otherwise, benefit of bail shall immediately be withdrawn.
9. The applicant shall mark his presence on first Sunday of every month before the concerned police station between 10:00 am to 2:30 pm till conclusion of trial.
7. Application stands allowed and disposed of.
8. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance from the office of this Court.
